title: Cogni node/service catalog entry
description: task.0374 — single declaration site for nodes and node-shaped services. Consumed by image-tags.sh, detect-affected.sh, ApplicationSet generators, and per-workflow decide jobs. See docs/spec/ci-cd.md axiom 16 (CATALOG_IS_SSOT).

allOf.$comment: task.5025 — every node carries the stable wallet binding used to project an env-local users row, plus exactly one activity_env. activity_env is the singleton environment allowed to ingest Git receipts and run epoch schedules.
ACTIVITY_ENV_IS_DEPLOYED — JSON Schema cannot use $data references portably, so enumerate the three valid membership implications.

REPO_SPEC_IS_IDENTITY_SSOT — node_id lives in nodes/<name>/.cogni/repo-spec.yaml (the web3-anchored authority). A SUBMODULE node (source_repo set) has an unreadable-from-parent repo-spec at render time, so it carries a drift-gated node_id PROJECTION here (verify-scheduler-endpoints.sh asserts catalog.node_id == repo-spec.node_id). An IN-REPO node must NOT duplicate it — its repo-spec is readable.
Deploy branches are k8s/Argo per-env state. type:infra (e.g. litellm) deploys via Compose-on-VM (deploy-infra.sh resolves a content-hash tag), so it has no deploy branches.
Artifact rows with source_repo publish image_repository:sha-<sourceSha>. If source_repo is not this repo, the operator consumes the artifact by digest and does not build it.
task.5052 — compute_egress_cidrs is env-scoped through the row's own envs[]: the renderer unions declarations across rows deployed to an env, so a row declaring egress CIDRs must declare envs.
story.5016 — off-cluster placement is operator-owned, node-only policy; source_repo supplies the immutable node artifact lineage.

name.description: Catalog entry name. Used as image-tag suffix base, Argo Application name suffix, and deploy-branch suffix. Filename must match name.yaml.

type.description: node = full node app (operator/poly/resy); service = supporting k8s service (scheduler-worker); infra = shared VM-infra image built in CI but deployed via Compose-on-VM (litellm). node+service deploy via Argo; infra is content-hash tagged and resolved by deploy-infra.sh.

node_port.description: task.5078 — k3s Service NodePort the edge Caddy reverse-proxies to (host.docker.internal:<node_port>). Required for type:node. CATALOG_IS_SSOT: render-caddyfile.sh bakes it into the generated Caddyfile and deploy-infra.sh / provision-env-vm.sh skip per-node edits. Must equal the per-env overlay Service nodePort.

dockerfile.description: Repo-relative path to the build Dockerfile.

build_context.description: Docker build context (repo-relative). Defaults to '.' (repo root) for node/service images that COPY from the monorepo. type:infra images with a self-contained context (e.g. litellm) set their own dir so the Dockerfile stays context-relative and its content-hash is stable.

image_tag_suffix.description: Tag suffix appended to base tags in GHCR. Empty for the historically-unsuffixed operator target; '-<name>' otherwise.

migrator_tag_suffix.description: Tag suffix for the per-node migrator image alias. Empty if this entry has no migrator.

path_prefix.description: task.0374 — repo path prefix that maps changed files to this target. detect-affected.sh uses this to compute the matrix shape. Must end with /.

source_repo.description: Artifact source repository clone URL. It names the build plane; deploy lanes resolve image_repository:sha-<sourceSha> to a digest.

node_id.description: Drift-gated projection of a SUBMODULE node's repo-spec node_id (UUID). Present only on submodule rows (source_repo set), where the repo-spec is unreadable from the parent at render time. verify-scheduler-endpoints.sh asserts it == nodes/<name>/.cogni/repo-spec.yaml; repo-spec is the identity SSOT.

image_repository.description: Required with source_repo. GHCR repository for the deployable artifact, resolved at sha-<sourceSha>. Prefer ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo> for a single primary artifact or deployable-shaped suffixes such as -app/-worker when the repo publishes multiple artifacts.

envs.description: task.5017/5025 — the non-empty per-env deploy set: which environments deploy this node. Consumed by scripts/ci/render-node-appset.sh and scripts/ci/reconcile-node-substrate.sh. deploy ⊆ provisioned: an env only deploys nodes it lists. Individual env membership is independent, but the final environment cannot be removed; full decommission is a separate lifecycle operation.

deployment_provider.description: Operator-owned per-environment app placement. Omitted environments preserve the k3s default; akash routes only the node app workload through the off-cluster ComputeWorkload reconciler.

activity_env.description: task.5025 — singleton environment that owns activity ingestion and epoch scheduling for this node. Must also be present in envs. V1 wizard births are fixed to candidate-a authority generation 1; changing authority is unsupported until a fenced quiesce/activate protocol exists. Deploying a node in multiple envs never permits multiple activity ledgers.

owner_wallet.description: Stable cross-environment owner binding. Each environment resolves or creates its own users.id by this wallet, then projects the OpenFGA node#admin ownership tuple; env-local user IDs are never copied through git.

compute_egress_cidrs.description: task.5052 (story.5016) — egress CIDRs of the decentralized-compute infrastructure (e.g. Akash provider NAT) that hosts THIS row's workload, allowed to reach the env VM's substrate ports (5432,5435,6379,4000,7233). Lives on the workload's own row — NOT per-env and NOT a shared infra row — because an egress IP is a property of where the workload runs: the per-env allowlist is the union of compute_egress_cidrs across rows whose envs[] contains that env, so decommissioning the workload (or trimming an env from envs[]) closes its holes with it. Rendered by scripts/ci/render-compute-egress-allowlist.sh into the allowlist consumed by infra/provision/cherry/harden-docker-public-ports.sh. Absent/empty = fail-closed: no off-cluster compute reaches the substrate ports. Provider egress NATs are multi-tenant — declare the narrowest CIDR (usually /32).

cidr.description: IPv4 CIDR (prefix length required; use /32 for a single egress IP).

comment.description: Single-line provenance: which provider(s) egress via this CIDR and the work item that added it.

is_primary_host.description: When true, this node serves the bare base domain (e.g. operator → https://${DOMAIN}). Defaults to false: every other node uses the ${name}-${DOMAIN} (multi-level domains) or ${name}.${DOMAIN} (TLD-style) convention. Consumed by host_for_node() in scripts/ci/lib/image-tags.sh. Exactly one catalog entry per repo should set this true.
